title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
blurb: In Depression-era Alabama, young Scout Finch watches her father, the lawyer Atticus, defend a Black man falsely accused of rape. A coming-of-age story about racial injustice, moral courage and the loss of childhood innocence.

author: George Orwell
blurb: Winston Smith rewrites history for the Party in a totalitarian superstate ruled by Big Brother, where surveillance never stops and even a thought can be a crime. A bleak warning about propaganda, censorship and the destruction of truth.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Quick-witted, quick-to-judge Elizabeth Bennet spars with the proud Mr Darcy while her mother schemes to marry off five daughters. A sharp, funny comedy of manners about class, first impressions and love in Regency England.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
blurb: Nick Carraway is drawn into the glittering Long Island world of the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby, who throws lavish parties hoping to win back Daisy Buchanan. A short, lyrical tragedy of the Jazz Age and the hollowness of the American Dream.

title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
blurb: The sailor Ishmael signs on to the whaler Pequod, whose captain Ahab is consumed by vengeance against the white whale that took his leg. An epic sea voyage about obsession, fate and humanity's struggle against nature.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J. D. Salinger
blurb: Expelled from prep school, sixteen-year-old Holden Caulfield drifts around New York City for a few days, railing against the phoniness of the adult world. A defining novel of teenage alienation, grief and the wish to protect innocence.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
blurb: Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy, dreams of treasure near the Egyptian pyramids and crosses the desert to find it. A short, fable-like story about following your dreams, listening to your heart and finding your purpose.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
blurb: In the future World State, people are engineered in hatcheries, conditioned from birth and kept content with pleasure and the drug soma. A dystopia where control comes through comfort rather than fear, questioning the price of stability and happiness.

title: The Lord of the Rings
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
blurb: The hobbit Frodo Baggins and a fellowship of companions set out to destroy the One Ring before the Dark Lord Sauron can reclaim it. The great epic of high fantasy: friendship, sacrifice and ordinary people standing against overwhelming evil.

title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
author: J. K. Rowling
blurb: On his eleventh birthday, orphaned Harry learns he is a wizard and is whisked off to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. A magical boarding-school adventure about friendship, courage and the first stirrings of a dark wizard's return.

title: The Kite Runner
author: Khaled Hosseini
blurb: Amir, a privileged boy in Kabul, betrays his loyal friend Hassan, and the guilt follows him through the Soviet invasion, exile in America and the rise of the Taliban. A moving story of friendship, fathers and sons, and redemption.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
blurb: Harari surveys the history of our species, from the cognitive revolution through farming and empire to science and capitalism. A provocative big-picture account of how shared myths let humans cooperate in huge numbers and dominate the planet.

title: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
blurb: The former First Lady recounts her childhood on Chicago's South Side, her career as a lawyer and her years in the White House. A warm, candid memoir about identity, family, ambition and finding your voice.

title: The Power of Habit
author: Charles Duhigg
blurb: Journalist Charles Duhigg explains the cue-routine-reward loop behind habits, drawing on neuroscience and stories from people, companies and social movements. Practical insight into why we do what we do and how habits can be changed.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
blurb: James Clear argues that tiny one-percent improvements compound into remarkable results, and lays out a practical system for building good habits and breaking bad ones. Focused on identity, environment design and making good behaviour obvious, attractive, easy and satisfying.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
blurb: Tara Westover grew up in a survivalist family in rural Idaho, never set foot in a classroom, and went on to earn a PhD from Cambridge. A gripping memoir about family loyalty, self-invention and the painful, transformative power of education.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
blurb: Alicia Berenson, a celebrated painter, shoots her husband and then never speaks another word. Psychotherapist Theo Faber becomes obsessed with uncovering her motive in a twisty psychological thriller with a shocking ending.

title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
author: Mark Manson
blurb: Mark Manson argues that chasing constant positivity makes us miserable, and that we should choose carefully what to care about instead. Blunt, profane, counterintuitive self-help about values, responsibility and accepting limits.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
blurb: Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman describes the two systems that drive how we think: fast, intuitive and emotional versus slow, deliberate and logical. A tour of cognitive biases and the systematic errors in human judgement and decision-making.

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
author: Stephen R. Covey
blurb: Stephen Covey presents a principle-centred approach to personal and professional effectiveness, from being proactive to beginning with the end in mind. A classic guide to character, priorities and working well with others.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
blurb: Orphaned and mistreated as a child, Jane Eyre becomes governess at Thornfield Hall and falls in love with its brooding master, Mr Rochester, who hides a terrible secret. A gothic romance about independence, integrity and a woman's insistence on equality.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
blurb: In St Petersburg, the impoverished former student Raskolnikov murders a pawnbroker to test a theory about extraordinary men, then is tormented by guilt and a patient investigator. A psychological novel about morality, conscience and redemption.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
blurb: Young scientist Victor Frankenstein brings a creature to life from dead matter, then abandons it in horror, and the lonely, eloquent creature seeks revenge. An early science-fiction and gothic horror classic about ambition, responsibility and what makes us human.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
blurb: A beautiful young man wishes his portrait would age in his place, and as he sinks into hedonism and cruelty the painting records every sin. A witty, decadent gothic tale about vanity, morality and the price of eternal youth.

title: Of Mice and Men
author: John Steinbeck
blurb: Two itinerant ranch hands, quick-witted George and the gentle, strong, childlike Lennie, dream of owning a small farm during the Great Depression. A short, heartbreaking novella about friendship, loneliness and broken dreams.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
blurb: Seven generations of the Buendía family live, love and fight in the mythical town of Macondo, where the miraculous and the everyday sit side by side. A landmark of magical realism about memory, solitude and the cycles of Latin American history.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
blurb: Sethe, who escaped slavery, lives in post-Civil War Ohio in a house haunted by the ghost of her dead baby daughter, until a mysterious young woman called Beloved arrives. A haunting, lyrical novel about the trauma of slavery, motherhood and memory.

title: The Road
author: Cormac McCarthy
blurb: A father and his young son walk south through a burned, ash-covered America after an unnamed catastrophe, scavenging for food and hiding from marauders. A spare, devastating post-apocalyptic story about love and hope at the end of the world.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
blurb: Kathy H. looks back on her years at Hailsham, a seemingly idyllic English boarding school, and slowly reveals the disturbing purpose for which she and her friends were raised. A quietly devastating novel about memory, love and mortality.

title: Life of Pi
author: Yann Martel
blurb: After a shipwreck, an Indian teenager named Pi survives 227 days in a lifeboat on the Pacific with a Bengal tiger called Richard Parker. A survival adventure that asks what we choose to believe and why we tell stories.

title: Where the Crawdads Sing
author: Delia Owens
blurb: Abandoned by her family, Kya Clark grows up alone in the marshes of coastal North Carolina, and years later becomes the prime suspect when a local golden boy is found dead. Part coming-of-age story, part nature writing, part romance and murder mystery.

title: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
blurb: On the night she decides to die, Nora Seed finds herself in a library between life and death, where every book lets her try a different version of her life. An uplifting, philosophical novel about regret, choices and what makes a life worth living.

title: Lessons in Chemistry
author: Bonnie Garmus
blurb: In the early 1960s, brilliant chemist Elizabeth Zott is pushed out of her research lab and becomes the unlikely star of a television cooking show that teaches science to housewives. A funny, feminist novel about sexism, single motherhood and refusing to compromise.

title: A Man Called Ove
author: Fredrik Backman
blurb: Ove is a grumpy, rule-obsessed widower in a quiet Swedish housing estate whose plans keep being interrupted by the lively new family next door. A funny, tender story about grief, community and unexpected friendship.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
blurb: Guy Montag is a fireman whose job is to burn books in a future America where reading is forbidden and people are numbed by wall-sized screens. A dystopian classic about censorship, conformity and the value of independent thought.

title: The Handmaid's Tale
author: Margaret Atwood
blurb: In the theocratic Republic of Gilead, which has replaced the United States, fertile women like Offred are forced to bear children for the ruling elite. A chilling dystopia about women's rights, religious extremism and resistance.

title: Station Eleven
author: Emily St. John Mandel
blurb: A flu pandemic wipes out most of humanity, and twenty years later a troupe of actors and musicians travels the Great Lakes region performing Shakespeare. A hopeful, elegiac post-apocalyptic novel about art, memory and what survives.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
blurb: Comfort-loving hobbit Bilbo Baggins is swept into a quest with the wizard Gandalf and thirteen dwarves to reclaim treasure from the dragon Smaug. A charming fantasy adventure about courage and home, and the prelude to The Lord of the Rings.

title: A Game of Thrones
author: George R. R. Martin
blurb: Noble houses scheme and go to war for the Iron Throne of the Seven Kingdoms, while an ancient threat stirs beyond the Wall in the far north. Gritty, political epic fantasy full of betrayal, morally grey characters and shocking deaths.

title: Mistborn: The Final Empire
author: Brandon Sanderson
blurb: In a world of falling ash ruled for a thousand years by the immortal Lord Ruler, street thief Vin discovers she can draw magical powers from metals and joins a crew plotting to overthrow him. An epic fantasy heist with an inventive magic system.

title: The Night Circus
author: Erin Morgenstern
blurb: A mysterious black-and-white circus that opens only at night hosts a secret magical duel between two young illusionists, Celia and Marco, who fall in love. A dreamy, atmospheric fantasy romance.

title: Circe
author: Madeline Miller
blurb: The witch Circe, daughter of the sun god Helios, is banished to an island where she hones her craft and crosses paths with Odysseus, Daedalus and the Minotaur. A feminist retelling of Greek mythology about power, solitude and transformation.

title: The Song of Achilles
author: Madeline Miller
blurb: Patroclus, an exiled young prince, tells of his love for Achilles from their boyhood to the Trojan War. A romantic, tragic retelling of the Iliad and Greek myth.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
blurb: On the desert planet Arrakis, sole source of the precious spice melange, young Paul Atreides is caught in a deadly struggle between noble houses and finds his destiny among the Fremen. Epic science fiction about politics, religion, ecology and power.

title: Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
blurb: Mathematician Hari Seldon uses psychohistory to predict the fall of the Galactic Empire and sets up a Foundation to shorten the dark age that will follow. A classic science fiction saga of ideas spanning centuries.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
blurb: Burned-out hacker Case is hired by a mysterious employer for one last job in cyberspace, with the augmented mercenary Molly at his side. The novel that defined cyberpunk: artificial intelligence, megacorporations and virtual reality.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
author: Douglas Adams
blurb: Seconds before Earth is demolished to make way for a hyperspace bypass, Arthur Dent is rescued by his friend Ford Prefect, a researcher for a galactic travel guide. Absurd, hilarious comic science fiction.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
blurb: Ryland Grace wakes alone on a spaceship with no memory and slowly realises he is on a desperate mission to save Earth from a microbe that is dimming the sun. A funny, science-heavy space adventure about problem-solving and an unlikely friendship.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
blurb: Stranded on Mars after his crew leaves him for dead, astronaut and botanist Mark Watney uses engineering, science and gallows humour to survive until rescue. A gripping survival story built on problem-solving.

title: The Three-Body Problem
author: Liu Cixin
blurb: During China's Cultural Revolution a secret military project sends signals into space and makes contact with an alien civilisation; decades later, leading scientists begin dying mysteriously. Hard science fiction about physics, first contact and humanity's fate.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
blurb: On their fifth wedding anniversary Amy Dunne vanishes, and her husband Nick becomes the prime suspect as the media frenzy grows. A dark, twisty psychological thriller about marriage, lies and unreliable narrators.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
blurb: Disgraced journalist Mikael Blomkvist and the brilliant, tattooed hacker Lisbeth Salander investigate a decades-old disappearance in a wealthy Swedish family. A dark Nordic crime thriller about violence against women, corruption and secrets.

title: The Da Vinci Code
author: Dan Brown
blurb: Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon is pulled into a murder at the Louvre and a race across Europe to uncover a secret about the Holy Grail. A fast-paced conspiracy thriller full of codes, art history and puzzles.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
blurb: Ten strangers are lured to an isolated island off the Devon coast and are killed one by one, following a sinister nursery rhyme. Agatha Christie's ingenious, chilling whodunit.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: Sherlock Holmes and Dr Watson investigate the death of Sir Charles Baskerville and the legend of a spectral hound haunting the bleak Dartmoor moors. A classic detective mystery with gothic atmosphere.

title: The Thursday Murder Club
author: Richard Osman
blurb: Four pensioners in a retirement village meet every week to puzzle over unsolved cold cases, until a real murder happens on their doorstep. A cosy, witty British mystery about friendship and growing old.

title: Big Little Lies
author: Liane Moriarty
blurb: A death at a school trivia night in a seaside Australian town is unravelled through the stories of three mothers and the secrets they keep. A darkly comic domestic mystery about friendship, gossip and domestic violence.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
blurb: Told through letters and diaries: solicitor Jonathan Harker travels to Transylvania and discovers that his client, Count Dracula, is a vampire bound for England. The gothic horror classic that defined the vampire legend.

title: The Shining
author: Stephen King
blurb: Jack Torrance takes a job as winter caretaker of the isolated Overlook Hotel with his wife and psychic son Danny, and the hotel's evil presence starts to work on Jack's mind. A terrifying horror novel about addiction, isolation and madness.

title: Mexican Gothic
author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
blurb: In 1950s Mexico, glamorous socialite Noemí travels to a decaying mansion in the countryside after a disturbing letter from her newlywed cousin. A creepy gothic horror novel about colonialism, eugenics and a family's rotten secrets.

title: The Haunting of Hill House
author: Shirley Jackson
blurb: Four people gather at a notorious mansion to study the paranormal, and lonely, fragile Eleanor begins to feel that the house wants her. A subtle, psychological haunted-house classic.

title: Outlander
author: Diana Gabaldon
blurb: In 1946, nurse Claire Randall touches a standing stone in the Scottish Highlands and is thrown back to 1743, where she is caught up in clan politics and falls for the Highlander Jamie Fraser. A sweeping time-travel historical romance.

title: The Notebook
author: Nicholas Sparks
blurb: An old man reads a love story from a worn notebook to a woman in a nursing home: the tale of Noah and Allie, a young couple separated by class and reunited years later in North Carolina. A tear-jerking romance about enduring love and memory.

title: Me Before You
author: Jojo Moyes
blurb: Louisa Clark takes a job caring for Will Traynor, a wealthy, sardonic man left paralysed after an accident, and their relationship changes them both. A funny, heartbreaking romance about love and choice.

title: Beach Read
author: Emily Henry
blurb: Two novelists with writer's block, a romance author and a literary fiction writer, spend a summer in neighbouring lake houses and agree to swap genres. A witty, emotional romantic comedy about grief and second chances.

title: All the Light We Cannot See
author: Anthony Doerr
blurb: A blind French girl, Marie-Laure, and a German orphan with a gift for radios, Werner, see their paths converge in occupied Saint-Malo during the Second World War. A lyrical historical novel about goodness amid war.

title: The Book Thief
author: Markus Zusak
blurb: Narrated by Death, the story follows Liesel, a foster girl in Nazi Germany who steals books and shares them with her neighbours and the Jewish man hidden in her basement. A moving tale about words, kindness and loss in wartime.

title: Wolf Hall
author: Hilary Mantel
blurb: Thomas Cromwell, a blacksmith's son, rises to become Henry VIII's most powerful adviser as the king seeks to annul his marriage and wed Anne Boleyn. Booker-winning historical fiction about Tudor power and politics.

title: The Nightingale
author: Kristin Hannah
blurb: Two sisters in Nazi-occupied France take different paths: Vianne protects her family at home while Isabelle joins the Resistance and guides downed airmen to safety. A moving historical novel about women's courage in war.

title: The Hunger Games
author: Suzanne Collins
blurb: In the nation of Panem, Katniss Everdeen volunteers to take her younger sister's place in a televised fight to the death between teenagers. A gripping young adult dystopian adventure about survival, inequality and rebellion.

title: The Fault in Our Stars
author: John Green
blurb: Hazel, a sixteen-year-old with terminal cancer, falls in love with Augustus Waters, whom she meets at a support group. A funny, heartbreaking young adult love story about illness and mortality.

title: The Giver
author: Lois Lowry
blurb: In a seemingly perfect community without pain or choice, twelve-year-old Jonas is chosen to receive the memories of the past and discovers the dark truth behind his society. A young adult dystopian classic.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
author: Jared Diamond
blurb: Jared Diamond asks why Eurasian societies came to conquer others, and argues that geography, domesticable plants and animals, and disease, not race, shaped the course of history. A sweeping account of how human societies developed.

title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
author: Mary Beard
blurb: Classicist Mary Beard tells the story of ancient Rome from its mythical founding to 212 CE, when citizenship was extended to all free people in the empire. A lively, myth-busting history of Rome and its people.

title: Team of Rivals
author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
blurb: Historian Doris Kearns Goodwin shows how Abraham Lincoln brought his political rivals into his cabinet and led them through the Civil War. A history of political genius and leadership in a time of crisis.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
blurb: Physicist Stephen Hawking explains the big bang, black holes, the nature of time and the search for a unified theory, for readers with no background in physics. The landmark popular science book about the cosmos.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
blurb: Richard Dawkins argues that evolution is best understood from the gene's point of view, with living organisms as vehicles that genes build to copy themselves. A classic of popular science that also introduced the idea of the meme.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
blurb: Carl Sagan journeys through the history of science and the universe, from ancient astronomers to the search for life beyond Earth. A poetic, wonder-filled exploration of space and our place in it.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
author: Rebecca Skloot
blurb: Henrietta Lacks, a poor Black tobacco farmer, had cancer cells taken without her consent in 1951; they became the HeLa line behind countless medical breakthroughs. Science writing about medical ethics, race and the family left behind.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank
blurb: The diary kept by a Jewish teenager hiding with her family in a secret annex in Amsterdam during the Nazi occupation. An honest, moving record of adolescence, fear and hope during the Holocaust.

title: When Breath Becomes Air
author: Paul Kalanithi
blurb: Neurosurgeon Paul Kalanithi, diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer at thirty-six, reflects on medicine, mortality and what makes a life meaningful. A short, profound memoir about facing death.

title: Born a Crime
author: Trevor Noah
blurb: Comedian Trevor Noah recounts growing up in South Africa under apartheid as the son of a Black mother and a white father, whose relationship was illegal. A funny, moving memoir and a tribute to his fearless mother.

title: Shoe Dog
author: Phil Knight
blurb: Nike founder Phil Knight recounts the company's early years, from selling imported Japanese running shoes out of his car to building a global brand. A candid business memoir about risk, persistence and entrepreneurship.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
blurb: Psychiatrist Viktor Frankl recounts his time in Nazi concentration camps and describes logotherapy, his approach built on finding meaning even in suffering. A short, powerful book about purpose and resilience.

title: Quiet
author: Susan Cain
blurb: Susan Cain argues that Western culture undervalues introverts and shows how introversion fuels creativity and leadership. Psychology plus practical advice for introverts at work, at school and at home.

title: Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
author: Robert B. Cialdini
blurb: Psychologist Robert Cialdini explains six principles of persuasion, including reciprocity, social proof, authority and scarcity, and how to resist being manipulated by them. A classic on the psychology of persuasion, sales and marketing.

title: The Body Keeps the Score
author: Bessel van der Kolk
blurb: Psychiatrist Bessel van der Kolk explains how trauma reshapes the brain and body, and explores treatments from neurofeedback to yoga. A landmark book on trauma, PTSD and healing.

title: Mindset: The New Psychology of Success
author: Carol S. Dweck
blurb: Psychologist Carol Dweck contrasts the fixed mindset with the growth mindset, the belief that ability can be developed through effort and learning. Research-based insight into learning, parenting, sport and success.

title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
blurb: Cal Newport argues that the ability to focus without distraction on demanding work is rare and valuable, and gives rules for cultivating it. Productivity advice for a world of email, meetings and social media.

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
blurb: Spiritual teacher Eckhart Tolle teaches that freedom from anxiety and suffering comes from living fully in the present moment instead of in our thoughts. A guide to mindfulness and spiritual awakening.

title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
blurb: Dale Carnegie's enduring advice on making people like you, winning others to your way of thinking and leading without resentment, built on genuine interest and appreciation. A classic of communication and people skills.

title: Zero to One
author: Peter Thiel
blurb: PayPal co-founder Peter Thiel argues that real progress comes from creating new things rather than copying, and that startups should aim to build monopolies. Contrarian ideas about startups, innovation and building the future.

title: The Lean Startup
author: Eric Ries
blurb: Eric Ries presents a method for building startups through rapid experiments, minimum viable products and validated learning. A practical guide to entrepreneurship and innovation under uncertainty.

title: Good to Great
author: Jim Collins
blurb: Jim Collins and his research team studied companies that leapt from average results to sustained excellence and identified what set them apart, from humble leadership to disciplined focus. A management classic.

title: Freakonomics
author: Steven D. Levitt and Stephen J. Dubner
blurb: Economist Steven Levitt and journalist Stephen Dubner use data to answer surprising questions, from cheating schoolteachers to the economics of drug dealing. Popular economics about incentives and hidden causes.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
blurb: The private notes of the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius, written to himself about duty, mortality and self-discipline. The essential text of Stoic philosophy and a guide to living calmly.

title: Sophie's World
author: Jostein Gaarder
blurb: Fourteen-year-old Sophie receives mysterious letters that introduce her to the history of philosophy, from Socrates to Sartre, while her own reality begins to blur. A novel that doubles as a beginner's guide to philosophy.

title: The Myth of Sisyphus
author: Albert Camus
blurb: Albert Camus asks whether life is worth living in an absurd universe without inherent meaning, and answers with revolt, freedom and passion: one must imagine Sisyphus happy. An essential essay of existentialism and absurdism.

title: Steve Jobs
author: Walter Isaacson
blurb: Drawing on interviews with Jobs, his family, colleagues and rivals, Walter Isaacson portrays the Apple co-founder's genius, intensity and difficult personality. A story of creativity, technology and innovation.

title: Into the Wild
author: Jon Krakauer
blurb: Jon Krakauer reconstructs the life of Christopher McCandless, who gave away his savings, hitchhiked to Alaska and died alone in the wilderness. A haunting account of adventure, idealism and the pull of nature.
